overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation in the August 29 notice, which needn't name specific abatement applicants. It declined to review draft minutes, and noted the Board failed to respond to the complaint, reminding it of required steps.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the August 29 meeting notice was insufficiently specific because it did not identify the tax abatement applicants or properties to be discussed in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: It was therefore sufficient for the meeting notice to state generally that the Board was considering applications for abatement or exemption under chapter 59, section 60, and the Board did not violate the law by not listing on the notice for its August 29 meeting the specific applications to be discussed in executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the August 29 executive session minutes were insufficient because they did not identify the abatement applications discussed or record the vote on each.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review the sufficiency of minutes that are in draft form at the time a complaint is filed, as the public body may revise the minutes at any point prior to approval to correct inaccuracies or add
